title: Outline: section tree, moving sections and chapters, export bookmarks
instructions: Goal: a notebook with several PDFs shows one section per PDF in the bookmarks panel, with the PDF's own outline and the user's bookmarks inside; sections and chapters can be moved by dragging; the PDF export writes the same tree as PDF bookmarks. src/shared/outline.js already has mapPdfOutline (keep it and its tests). Read docs/NOTES-OUTLINE.md and src/shared/format.js (page and source fields) first. (1) Extend src/shared/outline.js with buildOutline(sources, pages, pdfOutlines). The bookmarks panel becomes a tree: one section per PDF in the notebook (in the order its first page appears), named after sources[key].name or the file name without '.pdf'; under it the PDF's own outline (pdfOutlines[key], already mapped with mapPdfOutline) and the user's bookmarked pages of that section in page order (title = bmTitle or 'Page n', n = 1-based position in the notebook). Pages that are not from a PDF (blank, ruled) belong to the section of the nearest PDF page above them; such pages before the first PDF page form a section 'Notes'. Return [{ kind: 'section', key, title, pageId (first page), items: [...] }] with outline entries { kind: 'outline', ... } and bookmarks { kind: 'bookmark', pageId, title }. Tests in test/unit/shared/outline.test.js: two PDFs, pages moved between them, bookmarks in both, notes before the first PDF, a notebook without PDFs (one 'Notes' section, bookmarks only). (2) Extend src/shared/outline.js with moveRange(pages, fromId, toIdExclusive, beforeId) and rangeOf(tree, entry). Dragging a section or chapter in the sidebar moves all its pages. rangeOf returns { fromId, toIdExclusive } for a tree entry: from its page to the page of the next entry of the same or a higher level (or the end). moveRange returns a NEW pages array with that run of pages moved before beforeId (null = to the end); pages keep their order inside the run; moving a run before one of its own pages returns the input order unchanged. Do not mutate inputs. Tests: move the second PDF section before the first, move a chapter inside its section, move to the end, no-op cases, and that buildOutline on the result still lists every bookmark once. (3) Extend src/shared/outline.js with outlineForExport(tree, pages). The PDF export will write the sidebar tree as PDF bookmarks. Return a flat list [{ title, level, pageIndex (0-based position in pages) }] in tree order; skip entries whose page is no longer in pages; titles at most 200 characters, never empty ('Page n' fallback); levels start at 0 and never jump by more than one from one entry to the next (clamp). Tests in test/unit/shared/outline.test.js. Rules: CommonJS with 'use strict'. src/shared stays pure: only ./ requires, no window, document, navigator, process or Buffer (test/unit/shared/shared-guard.test.js). Do not mutate inputs. Comments say why. Neutral English examples only. Tests with node:test and node:assert: every rule above plus edge cases and one realistic end-to-end case of the whole module. Run node --test on your test file and npm test if you can, and say exactly which ran. title: Scroll and zoom: render plan, pixel-budget cache and scroll velocity
instructions: Goal: long PDFs scroll without blank or blurry pages: pages on screen first, the next ones in the scroll direction prefetched, previews while moving, sharp pages when still, and a cache that never drops what is on screen. viewer.js (readable, do not change) keeps rendered pages in an LRU cache limited to 28 million pixels. (1) Add src/shared/scroll-velocity.js with createVelocityTracker({ windowMs = 120 }): add(t, y) records the scroll position y at time t (ms, increasing); velocity(t) returns px per ms from a least-squares line through the samples of the last windowMs (0 with fewer than 2 samples, or when the newest sample is older than windowMs at time t - the scroll has stopped); reset(). Keep at most 32 samples. Tests in test/unit/shared/scroll-velocity.test.js: steady scrolling, a stop, a reversal, irregular timestamps, many samples. (2) Add src/shared/render-plan.js with planRender(state). state: { pages: [{ index, top, height, width }] (screen px at the current zoom), viewTop, viewHeight, zoom, dpr, moving: boolean (scroll or zoom gesture in progress), velocityY (px per ms, + = down), cached: { [index]: scale }, maxCanvasPx: 16e6 }. Return an ordered list [{ index, scale, reason }]: pages intersecting the view first (by distance of their centre to the view centre), then up to 2 pages ahead in the direction of motion (velocity sign; both directions when |velocityY| < 0.05), then 1 page behind. Target scale = zoom * dpr, reduced so width*height*scale^2 <= maxCanvasPx. While moving: a page with any cached bitmap is skipped (the stretched bitmap is shown), and pages without one get scale * 0.5 (fast preview, reason 'preview'). When not moving: a page is listed only if its cached scale is outside 0.97..1.04 of the target (reason 'sharp'). Never list a page twice. Tests in test/unit/shared/render-plan.test.js for each rule, including a fast fling (velocity 3) and a huge page hitting the pixel cap. (3) Add src/shared/bitmap-cache.js exporting class PixelCache(budget, { onEvict }). Rendered pages are canvases; this pure class only does the bookkeeping by key with { px (pixels), scale, value }. set(key, value, px, scale) replaces an entry (calling onEvict for the old value unless it is the same value); get(key) marks it recently used; has, delete, clear (onEvict for all), size, used. When used > budget: evict entries not in the protected set (protect(keys) - the pages on screen) by oldest use first; never evict a protected entry, even if that leaves the cache over budget (report it with overBudget()). An entry larger than the whole budget is not stored (onEvict called at once, set returns false). Tests in test/unit/shared/bitmap-cache.test.js: LRU order, protection, oversize entries, replacing with the same value, clear. Also one test that drives all three together over a simulated fling across a 200-page PDF and checks the plan stays within budget. title: Recognition: keep ragged columns apart in block detection
instructions: Goal: 'Make text editable' never joins two text columns into one line. docs/FINDING-blocks-more-tests.md shows findBlocks merging two columns with ragged inner edges (gaps of 39, 83 and 52 px between lines at the same height) into one block. First add that fixture as a failing test, then fix findBlocks: find column gaps as vertical white channels that run through several consecutive text lines (allow the channel to shift by a little per line), and cut blocks along them before the smear joins them; a single wide word gap inside one line must not split a paragraph. Keep every existing test in scan-blocks.test.js green, and add tests for: a justified two-column page, a table with borders, one paragraph with one wide gap, a heading over two columns, and a 3-column page. Keep findBlocks within 1.5x of its current time on a 1500 x 2000 page (add a timing test with a generous limit). The maintainer re-runs the OCR references afterwards. title: Extension: formulas in the PDF export and when copying out
instructions: Goal: exported PDFs show the set formulas exactly like the screen; copying a box to another program gives $...$ in plain text and rendered HTML. Implement exportImage for 'rich-paste:math' in src/extensions/rich-paste/export.js: render the KaTeX HTML into an SVG foreignObject with the KaTeX CSS and the needed fonts inlined as data URLs, draw it on a canvas at the requested scale, return { png, width, height, baseline } in the units of fontSize (baseline from the .katex-html base box), colour from the style; if the canvas turns out tainted, say so and fall back to drawing the KaTeX output with canvas text (document the choice). Cache by source + size + colour + scale inside the extension. Unit tests: cache keys, size and baseline maths with stubbed measurements, colour handling. e2e: a box with an inline and a display formula -> export PDF -> pdftotext must not contain the LaTeX source and pdfimages (or the page render) shows the formula area inked at the right place (compare with the on-screen box position within 2 pt; use the e2e flow of test/e2e/extensions-host.js: inlineImages + exportTo); Ctrl+C on the box puts $...$ in text/plain. Read docs/EXTENSIONS.md first and follow it. If src/renderer/extensions.js or test/unit/extensions/fake-host.js is missing in your checkout, stop and report 'blocked'. ES module, default export with apiVersion 1, defaultEnabled false. Imports only from the extension's own folder, ../../shared/*.js and allowed packages; test/unit/main/extensions-guard.test.js must pass. Everything user-visible goes through host.ui.t() for translation. Unit tests with the fake host for all logic; an e2e test that goes through the user's path in the real app (switch on in Settings, use, undo, switch off) with check(...) lines like test/e2e/run.js. title: Study session: stitch scrolled screenshots into one page picture
instructions: Goal (ROADMAP-1.9, shortcut Ctrl+Alt+P): capture a whole web page or document by scrolling the window and joining the screenshots, for any app (no browser extension). Read docs/ROADMAP-1.9.md (section named in the goal) first. Add src/shared/scroll-stitch.js working on { width, height, data } RGBA frames: (1) fixedBands(frames) -> { top, bottom } rows that stay identical across frames (sticky header, footer, scrollbar strip excluded by columns that change), (2) overlap(a, b, { top, bottom }) -> the vertical shift of b against a (row hashes of the scrolling area, best match by a run of equal rows, tolerant to a few changed pixels per row, e.g. a blinking caret), or null when no overlap, (3) stitch(frames, { maxHeight = 30000 }) -> { image, shifts, stoppedAt } : header once at the top, footer once at the bottom, stops when two frames are equal (end of page) or no overlap is found, (4) plan(viewportHeight) -> scroll steps of 80 % so consecutive frames overlap. Tests with generated frames: plain text page, sticky header and footer, a page with an animated corner, end of page, no-overlap, 1 px rounding, a 20-frame page under 300 ms at 1280 px width. title: Handwriting: group strokes into lines and words and prepare them for recognition
instructions: Goal (ROADMAP-1.9 'Handwriting to text'): written ink becomes typed text at the same place, recognised locally; this task prepares the strokes. Read docs/ROADMAP-1.9.md (section named in the goal) first. Strokes are { id, p: [x, y, pressure, ...], s (width), c, t } (see src/shared/ink.js and format.js). Add src/shared/ink-lines.js: (1) classify(strokes) -> { text: [ids], other: [ids] } : long straight lines (underlines, rules), arrows, closed shapes and large drawings are other; dots and accents near text stay text. (2) lines(textStrokes) -> [{ ids, box, baseline, xHeight, slant }] ordered top to bottom, robust to slanted and slightly curved lines and to i-dots and t-bars above the line. (3) words(line) -> gaps by the distribution of horizontal gaps (bigger than 0.6 x height). (4) toImage(line, strokes, { height = 64 }) -> { width, height, data } Uint8 grayscale, deslanted, baseline at 3/4, stroke width scaled, white background, for an image model; toSequence(line) -> resampled points (equal distance, normalised by xHeight) with pen-up flags, for a sequence model. (5) placeText(line) -> { x, y, fs } for the typed text box (fs from xHeight). Tests with generated handwriting-like strokes: two lines, slant 15 degrees, dots and bars, an underline and an arrow as other, word gaps, image size and baseline.
